thread:
Olivia: FYI billing panel shows a sudden jump in embedding charges for some enterprise tenants starting around the new clientlib rollout. embedding unit count up ~6x but total raw tokens barely moved.
Sam: I pulled traces. transform service classification looks off for a subset of events. v3 client adds a billing_context block but sometimes omits content_type. transform currently prefers content_type and defaults to text -> likely misclassifying embeddings as text (or reversed) depending on earlier logic.
Ravi: Reproduced locally with a v3 sample payload: billing_context={kind: "embedding", dims:1536}, content_type: null -> mapped unit_type=text_tokens. downstream aggregator applies separate pricing for embedding vs token units, so the mismatch caused unexpected charge aggregation.
Marta: Confirmed. we have thousands of events per minute with that shape across 7 tenants. finance ran a quick pivot and saw charge buckets move to embedding for older events after some downstream enrichment, doubling the perceived embedding counts.
Olivia: Immediate mitigation options? patch transform to prefer billing_context.kind when present, or add a tolerant rule: if billing_context.kind == embedding then force unit_type=embedding.
Sam: I prefer the minimal rule to reduce risk: if billing_context exists and kind==embedding -> set unit=embedding; otherwise keep existing logic. No change to content_type precedence otherwise.
Ravi: Implemented PR with the small conditional. also added metric counter transform.classifier.rule_applied:{original,final}. will gate under feature flag and canary 5% of tenants.
Marta: How do we avoid double-counting when backfilling? finance will run comparisons and we must mark reprocessed events so they don't auto-commit to invoices. propose tag reprocess=true and write to staging_ledger table.
Olivia: Agreed. rollout plan: 1) deploy mapping fix to canary (5%) 2) monitor per-tenant ledger delta and transform.classifier.rule_applied 3) run selective backfill on whitelist tenants and mark reprocessed events 4) if stable, expand to 25% then 100% over a few hours. rollback criteria: any tenant >$500/day with invoice delta >1% or aggregator lag >30s.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: transform/prefer-billingcontext -> canary (5%) commit b4c2d1 in 3 mins.
Sam: I'll add Grafana panels: a) per-tenant embedding_units vs embedding_charge_count, b) classifier.override_rate, c) ledger_write_latency. Wire alert for per-tenant divergence >2%.
Marta: Drafted SQL for finance to reconcile recent history:
```sql
SELECT tenant_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN unit_type='embedding' THEN units ELSE 0 END) AS embedding_units,
  SUM(CASE WHEN reported_bucket='embedding' THEN charge_units ELSE 0 END) AS embedding_charges,
  SUM(charge_amount) AS total_charges,
  COUNT(*) AS event_count
FROM billing_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '72 hours'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY embedding_units DESC
LIMIT 100;
```
Marta: Uploaded the snapshot to FIN-487 and tagged CS so they can pre-empt any customer questions.
Ravi: Canary live. initial metric: transform.classifier.rule_applied shows ~0.03% hits as expected. embedding counts for canary tenants now align with raw dims.
metering-bot: Alert: billing:unit_mix panel reports +11% embedding_charge_count at 08:12 UTC (aggregate).
Sam: I see the alert on aggregate. per-whitelist tenants are stable. likely the surge includes historical events and non-canary tenants.
Olivia: Proceed with backfill for top-10 affected tenants only, mark reprocessed items, and produce staging report for finance. Ravi can run the job tonight?
Ravi: I can run the backfill for the whitelist. ETA ~2 hours for job to complete; will run with rate limit to avoid load spikes and write status to ops-log.
Sam: Also add a temporary derived metric embedding_charge_delta = embedding_charge_count - embedding_units to surface the discrepancy. Hook an alert if delta > 5% for any tenant over 1 hour.
Marta: CS and Finance are on standby. I've prepared suggested customer communications and credit templates if we need to issue adjustments.
Olivia: Postmortem owners: Olivia will draft root cause and timeline, Ravi will include code diff and rollout notes, Sam will include dashboard/alert changes, Marta will include finance reconciliation and customer comms.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: transform/prefer-billingcontext @ canary-topic (5%).
Ravi: Early telemetry looks clean. classifier.override_rate stabilizing. starting scheduled backfill for whitelist tenant list A; tagging each reprocessed event with reprocess=true and write_status=pending.
metering-bot: Info: backfill job started for 10 tenants at 08:40 UTC.
Olivia: Keep this thread updated with any anomalies. we'll reconvene after backfill completes and decide on wider rollout. thanks everyone. :folded_hands:
